Here’s the complete 12-week program summary for your 29-year-old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement. All work is pain-free range only, no overhead loading, neutral/semi-neutral grips favored, and progress is via load/density/tempo—not ROM. Coordinate changes with her physio.

Weekly structure
- Strength: 3 upper-body sessions/week (A, B, C)
- Cardio: 2 sessions/week (Z2 + tempo)
- Hangboard/tech prep: Integrated in Phases 2–4 (mostly in Session C or a short standalone)
- Mobility: Daily micro-sequence + targeted drills 2–3x/week
- Saturday finisher: 12–20 min, shoulder-safe, fun conditioning (after Session C)
- Recovery: 7–9 h sleep, hydration, cooldowns, pain rules
- Nutrition: Body recomposition (small deficit), performance-focused timing

Phases at a glance
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Mechanics, scap control, isometrics, horizontal push/pull base. No overhead loading.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Heavier horizontal strength, partial-range landmine press, start hangboard (feet-on, jug/large edge), begin easy technique.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Intensified strength, denser pulling, partial low-angle “vertical” pulls (below shoulder), progressed hangboard density, stronger cardio.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Peak and taper. Highest specific density in Week 10–11, Week 12 taper to arrive fresh for a climbing trip.

Upper-body strength (3 sessions/week)
Session A: Horizontal Pull Emphasis + Cuff/Scap
- Main row pattern (chest-supported rows; neutral grip)
- Low-angle single-arm cable pulldown to chest (elbow below shoulder height; partial vertical)
- Face pull to chest-height (elbows below shoulder)
- Rotator cuff ER (0–45° abduction across phases)
- Scap depression holds; suitcase/farmer carries

Session B: Horizontal Push Emphasis + Row Variations
- DB floor press or low-incline neutral-grip press (pain-free depth)
- Push-up variation (elevation adjusted to comfort)
- Cable fly (low-to-mid, controlled eccentrics, stop short of end range)
- Rotator cuff IR (0–45° abduction across phases)
- Anti-rotation core (Pallof/press holds)

Session C: Unilateral Stability + Climbing Prep
- 1-arm chest-supported rows with pauses
- Landmine press in scapular plane (partial range, below shoulder height)
- Arm work (hammer curls, neutral triceps)
- Forearm/wrist conditioning
- Hangboard/technique block (from Phase 2 onward; feet-on; big holds → large edges)

Key loading and progression
- RPE 6–8 on main lifts; 2–3 reps in reserve, strict technique
- Sets/reps evolve from 4x8–10 (Phase 1 base) to 4–5x4–6 (Phases 3–4 strength), with tempo work (3–4 s eccentrics) and denser rests late in Phase 3
- Progress via reps then load (2–5%); reduce range at first sign of symptoms

Cardio (2x/week)
- Session 1: Long Z2 build
  - Weeks 1–3: 30–40 min
  - Weeks 4–6: 45–55 min
  - Weeks 7–9: 60–70 min
  - Weeks 10–12: 75–90 min (practice fueling: 30–45 g carbs/h + electrolytes)
- Session 2: Tempo/interval endurance
  - Early: Z2 with 1-min surges
  - Mid: 2 x 8–12 min tempo (RPE 6.5–7) with Z2 between
  - Late: 3 x 6–8 min ladders or 2 x 12 min tempo; or hilly Z2

Hangboard and climbing-specific prep (feet-on only unless cleared)
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Intro, 1–2x/week
  - 4–6 x 15–20s feet-on jug/large-edge hangs (RPE 5–6), 60–90s rest
  - 8–12 min easy traverses (slab/vertical), right hand ≤ shoulder height
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Density and endurance, 2x/week
  - Intermittent hangs: 2 rounds of 6–8 x (10–12s on/18–20s off) big edge, 2–3 min between rounds
  - Scap depression/protraction holds on jugs, 3 x 15–20s
  - Optional 6–10 min easy traverses (silent feet, flags)
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–11): Peak-specific density
  - Ladders: 3 ladders of 4 reps each at 8–10s on/12–15s off; 2–3 min between
  - Mixed circuits: jug ↔ big edge (optional medium edge if 100% symptom-free)
- Week 12 taper (Mon only)
  - 2 rounds of 5 x (8–10s on/20–25s off) big edge, RPE 5–6
  - 5–8 min easy technique; zero pump

Mobility (5–6 days/week, 8–12 min)
- Daily micro-sequence: open book, quadruped T-spine rock-backs, scapular CARs, posterior cuff cross-body, low-angle pec doorway, gentle wall slides to tolerated range, breathing reset
- Pre-session: T-spine foam roll, thread-the-needle, scap push-ups, band ER, wall slides
- Post-session: Low-angle pec stretch, posterior cuff, modified sleeper (only if pain-free), breathing
- Targeted 2–3x/week: low-trap raises, serratus roller slides, wall lift-offs, banded scap depression/protraction holds, neck/UT downregulation
- Lower-body/trunk (2–3x/week): hip 90/90, adductor rock-backs, ankle dorsiflexion lunges

Saturday finisher (12–20 min; rotate by phase)
- Phase 1: 15-min aerobic strength circuit (bike/walk, DB rack squat, chest-supported row, sled push, suitcase carry, Pallof)
- Phase 2: 16-min EMOM (bike sprint; landmine press; KB hinge or deadlift; chest-supported row)
- Phase 3: 18-min AMRAP (bike/row cals; sandbag clean to front rack reverse lunges; suitcase carry; landmine press; 10s feet-on hang; 1-arm chest-supported row)
- Phase 4: Density finisher
  - Option A: 12-min alternating EMOM (sled push; mixed carries)
  - Option B: 3-round circuit: bike 45s; landmine press 6/side; trap-bar DL 6–8; feet-on hangboard density micro-set

Nutrition (recomp)
- Calories: Bodyweight x 28–32 kcal/day starting range (small deficit 250–400 kcal)
  - Training days: BW x 30–32; Rest: BW x 28–30; adjust ±100–150 kcal every 2 weeks
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day
- Carbs: 2.5–4.5 g/kg/day, bias around training; intra-carb 15–30 g for long sessions
- Fat: 0.6–1.0 g/kg/day
- Timing: Pre (25–40 g protein + 30–60 g carbs), Post (25–40 g protein + 60–90 g carbs)
- Micros/supps: Collagen 10–15 g + vitamin C 30–60 min pre-rehab/hangs; omega-3 (1–2 g EPA+DHA), vitamin D per labs, creatine 3–5 g/day, hydration 30–35 ml/kg/day + 500–750 ml around training
- Monitoring: 0.25–0.5% BW loss/week, maintain or improve performance, adjust carbs first

Pain rules and substitutions
- Acceptable: 0–2/10 transient discomfort resolving within 24 h
- Not acceptable: Pinch, sharp pain, night pain, ROM loss next day → reduce ROM/load/volume 30–50% and notify physio
- Substitutions:
  - Floor/DB press → machine chest press neutral grip with limited ROM
  - Landmine press → cable press at chest height or isometric wall press
  - Chest-supported row → machine row with chest pad/neutral handles
  - Face pull → cable ER to chest-height

Peak/taper (Weeks 10–12 highlight)
- Week 10–11: Heaviest strength and hangboard density; cardio long Z2 75–80 min; fuel at or near maintenance on long days
- Week 12: Early-week primer only (short strength + light hang density + easy technique), then rest, hydrate, and increase carbs to maintenance/slight surplus. Begin climbing trip fresh.

Weekly layout example
- Mon: Upper A + mobility
- Tue: Cardio Z2 + mobility
- Wed: Upper B + targeted mobility
- Thu: Hangboard/technique short block or rest + mobility
- Fri: Cardio tempo/hills + mobility
- Sat: Upper C + hangboard/technique + finisher + post-session mobility
- Sun: Off/easy walk + breathing/mobility

This integrated plan builds upper-body strength safely, restores shoulder mechanics, develops aerobic and grip endurance, and peaks her capacity for Week 12 while protecting the right shoulder. Adjust loads/volume weekly to keep symptoms at zero and performance trending up.

Below is a 12-week upper-body strength program tailored for a recreational climber with right subacromial impingement, cleared for pain-free range only and no overhead loading. It uses a phased approach to reinforce shoulder mechanics, build strength through safe ranges, and progressively reintroduce climbing-relevant demands without provoking symptoms. It assumes full-gym access and ongoing communication with her physio. If any drill causes pain beyond mild, short-lived discomfort, regress or stop and consult the physio.

Global guidelines
- Frequency: 3 upper-body sessions/week (e.g., Mon–Wed–Sat). Optional low-intensity climbing technique or easy ARC sessions can be added starting Phase 2 if symptom-free (see notes).
- Pain rules: Stay in pain-free range. No overhead pressing, no end-range elevation or forced internal rotation across body. Keep scaps set and avoid anterior humeral glide.
- Tempo and control: Emphasize 2–3s controlled eccentrics on all shoulder work. Pause 1s in stable mid-range positions as needed.
- Progression: Use double progression (reps then load) while maintaining perfect form and pain-free movement.
- Warm-up each session (10–12 min): 
  - 5 min light cardio + thoracic mobility (cat-cow x10, thoracic rotations x8/side, foam roll T-spine 60–90s).
  - Scapular activation circuit (2 rounds): 
    1) Scapular wall slides to comfortable range x10 (stop before pain, no elevation past symptoms),
    2) Serratus punches with band (supine) x12,
    3) Prone Y (short range, thumbs up) x8, Prone T x10 (or cables) – keep range limited and pain-free.
  - Specific activation: Banded external rotation (ER) at 0–30° abduction x12/side, low trap setting (prone depression holds) 3x10s.
- Cooldown (5–8 min): Gentle pec doorway stretch (shoulder neutral, forearm on frame, mild), posterior cuff cross-body stretch (short of pain), breathing reset (3 min nasal breathing, long exhales).

Phases overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Pain-free strength base, scapular control, isometrics, horizontal pulling bias. No overhead loading.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Progress to heavier horizontal push/pull, introduce inclined and unilateral work within range, controlled isotonics, begin climbing-specific grip prep.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength progression with tempo and mid-range loading; add pain-free partial-range vertical pull variations (below shoulder height), anti-rotation core, more unilateral stability.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Consolidate strength, add power-tempo elements (fast concentric, slow eccentric), integrate climbing-pattern supersets, and prepare for safe return to more demanding climbing.

Session structure each week
- A: Horizontal Pull Emphasis + Cuff/Scap
- B: Horizontal Push Emphasis + Row Variations
- C: Unilateral Stability + Climbing-Specific Prep

Loading notes
- RPE 6–8 on main lifts unless noted; stop 2–3 reps shy of form breakdown or pain.
- Rest 60–120s for accessories, 90–150s for main lifts.
- Tempo notation example: 3-0-1 = 3s eccentric, no pause, 1s concentric.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 (Establish mechanics, isometrics, pain-free range)
Week 1
- Session A
  1) Chest-supported row (neutral grip) 4x8, 3-1-1, RPE 6–7
  2) Half-kneeling cable row (elbow stays below shoulder height) 3x10/side
  3) Isometric ER at 0° abduction (band), elbow by side: 3x20–30s/side
  4) Low-to-mid trap raise (incline bench 30°, thumbs up, short range) 3x10
  5) Serratus wall slide with band around forearms to tolerated range 3x8
  6) Farmer carry (suitcase) light, upright, ribcage down 4x20–30m/side

- Session B
  1) Push-up to elevated surface (bench), pain-free depth 4x6–8, 3-0-1
  2) Cable fly (low-to-mid, neutral grip), stop well before end-range 3x10–12
  3) Scap push-up (protraction/retraction only) 3x12
  4) Isometric IR at 0° abduction (towel roll at elbow) 3x20–30s/side
  5) Prone row to external rotation (light DB, short arc) 3x8
  6) Pallof press 3x10/side, 2-1-2

- Session C
  1) 1-arm chest-supported row (slow) 3x8/side
  2) Landmine press in scapular plane, partial range below shoulder height 4x6–8, 2-1-1 (ensure no pain; stop if symptoms)
  3) Biceps curl (EZ bar or DB, neutral grip) 3x10–12
  4) Triceps cable pressdown (rope, neutral) 3x12
  5) Wrist extensors: DB reverse wrist curl 2x15; Wrist flexors 2x15; Pron/sup rotation 2x12/side
  6) Forearm isometric pinch hold (plates) 3x20s

Week 2
- Keep exercises; add 1 rep per set on main lifts or +2–5% load if all pain-free and RPE ≤7. Isometrics progress to 25–35s holds. Add 1 set to scap/rotator work if tolerated.

Week 3
- Same structure; progress range slightly where comfortable (e.g., a bit deeper push-up). Introduce tempo variation: last set of rows 4s eccentric. Keep landmine press strictly below shoulder height.

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 (Strength building within safe ranges, incline work, controlled isotonics)
Week 4
- Session A (Row focus)
  1) Chest-supported row 5x6–8, 3-0-1, RPE 7–8
  2) Seated cable row (neutral, elbows 30–45° from torso) 4x8
  3) Banded ER at 30° abduction 3x12/side, 2-1-2
  4) Prone T raise (thumbs up) 3x10
  5) Serratus punches (cable or band, supine) 3x12–15
  6) Suitcase carry heavier 4x25–30m/side

- Session B (Horizontal push)
  1) DB floor press (neutral/semi-supinated grip) 5x5–6, 3-1-1
  2) Incline push-up (slightly lower bench height than Phase 1) 3x8–10
  3) Cable pec fly (low-mid) 3x10–12
  4) Isotonic IR 0–30° abduction 3x12/side
  5) Triceps rope extensions 3x10–12
  6) Anti-rotation press hold 3x20s/side

- Session C (Unilateral + climber prep)
  1) 1-arm cable row, split-stance 4x8/side
  2) Landmine press partial range 4x6–8, add slight arc forward for serratus, stay below shoulder level
  3) Hammer curls 3x10–12
  4) Wrist roller (flex/ext) 2 rounds
  5) Hangboard submax forearm isometrics: feet-on, big jug only, 3x20s, RPE hand/forearm 5–6, shoulders packed, elbows slightly bent; stop if shoulder discomfort appears.

Week 5
- Progress reps/load 2–5% as tolerated. Add 1 set to ER/IR or increase to 14–15 reps. Landmine press range only if symptom-free.

Week 6
- Introduce tempo set on floor press (last set 4s eccentric). Add 1–2 more hangboard sets if zero shoulder symptoms, still feet-on and low intensity.

Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 (Strength progression, partial vertical pulls below shoulder height, unilateral control)
Week 7
- Session A
  1) Chest-supported row 5x5–6, heavier
  2) 1/2 kneeling single-arm lat cable pulldown from low-to-chest line (do not exceed shoulder height), elbows in, 4x8/side
  3) Cable face pull to chest (low angle), elbows below shoulder height 3x12, 2-1-2
  4) ER at 45° abduction (towel at side) 3x10–12
  5) Scap depression holds on dip bars (no shoulder extension beyond neutral) 3x15–20s

- Session B
  1) DB neutral-grip bench on low incline (15–20°), pain-free depth, 5x5–6
  2) Push-up (elevated or floor if completely pain-free) 3x8–10
  3) Cable fly (mid) 3x10
  4) IR isotonic 30–45° abduction 3x12
  5) Pallof press kneeling 3x10/side

- Session C
  1) 1-arm chest-supported row with 2s pause at mid-range 4x8/side
  2) Landmine press with slight rotation from hips (anti-rotation core), keep humerus below shoulder height 4x6–8
  3) Biceps (incline hammer curl, modest incline) 3x10
  4) Triceps (cable, neutral) 3x10–12
  5) Hangboard feet-on: big jug + large edge, 4–5x15–20s, RPE 6–7, strict shoulder position

Week 8
- Progress loads 2–5%. Add eccentric emphasis on pulldown (3–4s). If any vertical pulling causes symptoms, revert to rows only.

Week 9
- Maintain or add one top set at RPE 8 on main lifts. Add light scapular CARs in warm-up (within pain-free range).

Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 (Consolidate strength, introduce controlled power-tempo, integrate climbing patterns)
Week 10
- Session A (Pull power-tempo)
  1) Chest-supported row: 4x5 heavy, then 2x6 at 60–65% with fast concentric, 3s eccentric
  2) 1-arm low-to-chest cable pulldown 4x6–8, 3s eccentric
  3) Face pull to chest 3x12
  4) ER at 45° abduction 3x10–12
  5) Scap depression holds 3x20s

- Session B (Push consolidation)
  1) DB floor press or low-incline neutral press 5x4–5, RPE 7–8
  2) Push-up (best tolerated variation) 3x8–12
  3) Cable fly slow eccentric 3x10
  4) IR isotonic 3x12–15
  5) Anti-rotation press hold 3x25s/side

- Session C (Integrated, climber-specific)
  1) 1-arm row with 2s isometric at end of safe range 4x6–8/side
  2) Landmine press alternating 3x8/side, crisp concentric, no pain
  3) Mixed grip block holds (feet-on) 4x15–20s
  4) Wrist roller x2; Pron/sup x12/side
  5) Farmer carry heavy 4x30–40m

Week 11
- Slight load bump on main lifts if RPE ≤7.5 last week. Keep tempo quality. If symptom-free, permit slightly larger ROM on low-incline press while staying below any pinching.

Week 12
- Peak week without testing:
  1) Rows: 5x4–5 at RPE 7–8
  2) Press: 5x4 at RPE 7–8
  - Keep accessory volumes, prioritize pristine control.
  - Optional tolerance check: add very light assisted vertical pull from low angle, only to below shoulder height, 2x12, stop immediately if any symptom.

Accessory and technique notes
- Scapular mechanics: Cue “ribcage down, sternum soft, shoulder blade glides around ribcage,” avoid shrugging. Think reach plus rotate for serratus drills.
- Elbow path: For push, 30–45° from torso; for rows, keep humeral head centered, avoid anterior glide at end-range.
- Grip: Favor neutral/semi-supinated grips. For climber prep, intensity stays low-moderate with feet support through entire 12 weeks unless physio OKs progression.

Pain management and red flags
- Acceptable: 0–2/10 transient discomfort resolving within 24 hours.
- Not acceptable: Pinching, sharp pain, night pain flare, ROM loss next day. If present, reduce ROM/load/volume by 30–50% and inform physio.

Progression summary
- Weeks 1–3: Build tolerance, learn positions, low-moderate loads.
- Weeks 4–6: Heavier horizontal strength, begin gentle landmine press and grip isometrics.
- Weeks 7–9: Add partial vertical pulls below shoulder height, increase unilateral demands.
- Weeks 10–12: Consolidate, add tempo power, maintain symptoms at zero.

Optional lower-intensity climbing integration
- If totally symptom-free following sessions in Weeks 4–6: 1–2 technical sessions/week, 30–45 min, easy circuits (well below limit), focus footwork and route reading. No dynamic moves, no gastons/overhead reaches on the right, stop with any shoulder awareness.
- By Weeks 8–12: If cleared, add 1 session of easy traversing and movement drills, keep effort ≤6/10.

Recovery, monitoring, and adjuncts
- Weekly check-in: Pain ratings during and 24h after, ROM notes, perceived effort, exercises that felt provocative.
- Soft-tissue: Light pec minor/lat/upper trap soft-tissue work 3–5 min as needed.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours, avoid right-side prolonged overhead sleep positions.
- Daily micro-dose (off days, 5–8 min): ER/IR band 2x12 each, serratus punches 2x12, thoracic rotation x6/side.
- Nutrition basics for tissue recovery and strength:
  - Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day across 3–5 meals.
  - Carbs around training for performance and recovery.
  - Omega-3 intake 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day if diet is low in fatty fish.
  - Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day; add 500–750 ml around training.
  - Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day if no contraindications.

Exercise substitutions (if any provoke symptoms)
- Floor press → machine chest press with neutral grip and restricted ROM.
- Landmine press → cable press at chest height or isometric press into wall.
- Chest-supported row → machine row with chest pad and neutral handles.
- Face pull → cable external rotation to chest-height.

Here’s a practical, climber-friendly body recomposition plan to pair with the 12-week program. Goal: lose fat gradually while gaining/maintaining lean mass and joint health. We’ll use a modest deficit, high protein, nutrient timing around training, and simple habit targets.

Key targets
- Calories: Bodyweight x 28–32 kcal/day as a starting range for a small deficit (about 250–400 kcal below maintenance). If you know her bodyweight, use:
  - Sedentary/non-training day: BW x 28–30
  - Training day: BW x 30–32
  - Adjust by 100–150 kcal every 2 weeks based on scale trend (see Monitoring).
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (anchor each meal with 25–40 g protein). Higher end if vegetarian or in larger deficit.
- Carbs: 2.5–4.5 g/kg/day, biased around training (pre/post) to support strength and shoulder rehab quality.
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day initially; can drift to 0.6–0.8 g/kg if needed to make room for carbs while keeping hormones and satiety in check.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day from fruits, veg, whole grains, legumes.
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day + 500–750 ml around training. Add electrolytes if she’s a heavy sweater.

Meal structure and timing
- 3 main meals + 1–2 snacks works well. Aim for:
  - Pre-training (60–120 min): 25–40 g protein + 30–60 g easily digested carbs + low fat/fiber. Example: Greek yogurt + banana + honey; turkey wrap; rice cakes + whey.
  - Post-training (0–2 hours): 25–40 g protein + 60–90 g carbs + produce; moderate sodium. Example: Chicken/rice/broccoli + soy sauce; smoothie with whey + oats + berries.
  - Evenly distribute remaining protein through other meals.
- Evening: Keep a protein-forward meal; include carbs if training late to aid recovery/sleep.

Macros example (for a 65 kg athlete; adjust to her BW)
- Calories: Training day ~2000–2150 kcal; Rest day ~1850–1950 kcal.
- Protein: 130–145 g
- Carbs: 210–260 g (higher on training days)
- Fat: 55–65 g (slightly lower on training days when carbs go up)

Food quality priorities
- Protein: Lean meats, fish, eggs/egg whites, Greek yogurt/skyr, cottage cheese, whey/plant protein, tofu/tempeh, legumes.
- Carbs: Rice, oats, potatoes, quinoa, whole-grain breads/wraps, fruit, lower-FODMAP veg around workouts if gut sensitive.
- Fats: Olive oil, avocado, nuts/seeds, fatty fish (salmon, trout), dark chocolate 70%+.
- Micronutrients for shoulder health: 
  - Collagen + vitamin C: 10–15 g collagen or gelatin 30–60 min pre-training with a vitamin C source (e.g., orange/kiwi) may support tendon/connective tissue.
  - Omega-3: 1–2 g/day EPA+DHA (or 3 fatty fish meals/week).
  - Calcium/vitamin D: 1000–1200 mg Ca/day from food; vitamin D per bloods (common range 1000–2000 IU/day).
  - Magnesium: 200–400 mg/day if sleep/muscle tension is an issue.

Week-by-week structure
- Weeks 1–2: Establish habits and baseline
  - Set calories at the low end of training/rest formulas. Hit protein minimum daily. Pre/post training fueling as above.
  - Build plate template: 1/2 veg/fruit, 1/4 lean protein, 1/4 starchy carb; add 1–2 thumb portions of healthy fats as needed.
  - Start food logging (3–5 days/week) or use hand-portion method if logging is stressful.
- Weeks 3–4: Dial in fueling around sessions
  - Increase carbs by ~20–30 g in the pre- and post-training window on heavy days if performance flags.
  - Keep rest days slightly lower carb, slightly higher fat.
  - Collagen + vitamin C protocol before upper-body sessions 2–3x/week.
- Weeks 5–6: Small adjustment block
  - If average weekly weight change is >0.5% loss, raise calories by 100–150 kcal (mostly carbs). If <0.25% loss and body comp isn’t improving, reduce by 100 kcal (mostly carbs/fats).
  - Keep protein steady.
- Weeks 7–9: Support higher training demands
  - Push carbs toward the higher end of the range on training days, especially before and after sessions. Keep fats on the lower end those days.
  - Consider intra-workout carbs (15–30 g from sports drink or juice + pinch of salt) for sessions >75 min.
- Weeks 10–12: Consolidate and prepare for next block
  - Hold a small deficit if strength is holding. If lifts stall or shoulder feels sluggish, add 100–150 kcal on training days.
  - Keep sleep and hydration top priority. Maintain collagen + vitamin C before rehab-heavy days.

Simple day templates
- Training day
  - Breakfast: Veg omelet + 2 egg whites + whole-grain toast + fruit
  - Snack (pre): Greek yogurt + banana + honey
  - Lunch (post): Chicken thigh, jasmine rice, mixed veg, olive oil; kiwi
  - Snack: Whey shake + rice cakes + peanut butter
  - Dinner: Salmon, sweet potato, asparagus; side salad
- Rest day
  - Breakfast: Skyr + berries + chia
  - Lunch: Tofu stir-fry with mixed veg, quinoa, sesame oil
  - Snack: Cottage cheese + apple + walnuts
  - Dinner: Turkey chili with beans; avocado; greens

Supplements (optional, evidence-based)
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day, any time. Supports strength and lean mass; safe for women.
- Whey or plant protein: To meet protein targets conveniently.
- Omega-3: 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day if fish intake is low.
- Vitamin D3: Dose per blood test or 1000–2000 IU/day general guidance.
- Collagen/gelatin: 10–15 g + 50–100 mg vitamin C pre-training as above.
- Caffeine: 1–3 mg/kg 30–45 min pre-session if desired; avoid late-day use.

Monitoring and adjustments

Here’s a shoulder-safe mobility plan to layer onto her program. It targets thoracic spine, scapular mobility/control, posterior cuff, and pec/lat restrictions common in subacromial impingement—without forcing overhead range. Keep all motions pain-free and submax; stop before any pinching.

How to use
- Frequency: 5–6 days/week in short doses (8–12 minutes). Place a brief sequence in the warm-up and a gentler version post-session or on off days.
- Intensity: Easy-to-moderate stretch sensation (3–5/10), never sharp. Breathe slowly through nose; 3–4 second exhales.
- Progression: Increase range only when it feels easy and symptom-free for 1–2 weeks. Prioritize quality over depth.

Daily micro-sequence (8–10 min, great on off days)
1) T-spine opener (sidelying open book)
   - 2 x 6–8 reps/side, slow inhale to rotate, exhale to settle. Hips/knees at 90°, keep shoulder below pain threshold.
2) Quadruped T-spine rock-back with reach
   - 2 x 6–8 reps/side. From all-fours, sit hips back, reach one arm forward on floor to a comfortable range, slight protraction, then return. No overhead pinch.
3) Scapular CARs (controlled articular rotations)
   - Standing or quadruped, 2 x 5 slow circles/side each direction: elevate → protract → depress → retract. Keep ribcage quiet; small, controlled circles.
4) Posterior cuff cross-body stretch (modified)
   - Arm across chest but keep shoulder blade set and humerus parallel to ground; stop before any pinch. 2 x 20–30s/side, gentle.
5) Pec minor doorway (low angle)
   - Forearm on frame with elbow near ribcage, not raised. Step through gently, 2 x 20–30s/side.
6) Lat/serratus wall slide to tolerated range
   - Forearms on wall, light band around wrists if tolerated, slide up only to pain-free height; emphasize upward rotation from scapula, not shrugging. 2 x 8–10 slow reps.
7) Breathing reset
   - Hooklying 90/90 or child’s pose with elbows on pads, 2–3 minutes of slow nasal breaths, long exhales to downshift tone.

Pre-session mobility (6–8 min add-on to warm-up)
- Foam roll T-spine: 60–90s, small upper-back extensions with ribs down.
- Thoracic rotations (thread the needle): 6/side.
- Scapular push-ups: 2 x 10, smooth protraction/retraction.
- Banded ER at 0–30° abduction: 1 x 12/side, 2–3s eccentrics.
- Wall slide to tolerated range: 1 x 8–10 with soft core and low traps engaged.

Post-session recovery (6–8 min)
- Low-angle pec doorway: 2 x 20–30s/side.
- Cross-body posterior cuff: 2 x 20–30s/side, gentle.
- Sleeper stretch (modified) if pain-free:
  - Sidelying, shoulder and elbow at 90°, roll body slightly forward to avoid pinch; gently guide forearm toward table until mild stretch in posterior shoulder, 2 x 20–30s. Skip if any impingement.
- T-spine breathing in child’s pose or croc breathing: 2–3 min.

Targeted drills 2–3x/week (when you have 12–15 min)
1) Scap upward-rotation groove (wall lift-off)
   - Forearms on wall, slight pressure, slide to tolerable height, then 1–2 cm lift-off for 3s, keeping ribs down and no shrug. 2 x 6–8 reps.
2) Prone low trap set + raise
   - On bench at 15–30°, thumbs up, slight depression, raise only through pain-free arc. 2–3 x 8–10, 3s lower.
3) Serratus foam roller slide with lift
   - Forearms on roller against wall, slide up to comfortable range while gently pressing forearms into roller; small lift at end-range if zero symptoms. 2 x 6–8.
4) Band-assisted scap depression/protraction holds
   - Light band overhead anchored forward at chest height; grip neutral with elbows slightly bent, step back to create light tension. Hold 10–15s depression, then 10–15s slight protraction, 3 rounds. Keep humerus below shoulder height.
5) Neck/upper trap downregulation
   - Gentle upper trap stretch: 20–30s/side.
   - First rib self-mob (strap/band) if taught by physio; otherwise skip.

Lower-body and trunk mobility for climbers (2–3x/week, 8–10 min)
- Hip 90/90 transitions: 2 x 6/side.
- Adductor rock-backs: 2 x 8–10/side.
- Ankle dorsiflexion lunges at wall: 2 x 10/side.
- Thoracic extension on bench with dowel at chest-height only: 2 x 8 gentle reps.

Mobility progressions by phase
- Phase 1–2: Keep ranges small; prioritize T-spine, scap CARs, pec minor, posterior cuff. No end-range loading or long lat stretches if they provoke.
- Phase 3 (intensified training): Maintain the daily micro-sequence; add targeted drills 2–3x/week. Emphasize serratus/low-trap work to support denser pulling and landmine pressing.
- Phase 4 (peak/taper): Keep mobility light and frequent. Short 5–8 min flows with breathing. Avoid aggressive stretching 48 hours before travel and big climbing days.

Technique cues to protect the subacromial space
- Ribs down, chin tucked slightly; avoid flared ribs during any overhead-leaning motions.
- Think “reach around the ribcage” (serratus) before “pull back” (rhomboids).
- Keep humeral head centered: elbow path 30–45° from torso; stop before any anterior glide or pinch.
- If a drill repeatedly provokes symptoms, remove it and substitute with T-spine or ribcage breathing until cleared.

Quick substitutions if any drill is provocative
- Wall slides hurt → swap for serratus punches and quadruped rock-back reaches.
- Sleeper stretch irritates → use cross-body stretch at lower angle or posterior capsule self-massage (ball) 60–90s light.
- Pec doorway bothers → switch to supine pec minor release with ball + breathing, or low incline foam pec stretch with arm by side.

Weekly placement example

- Tue: Cardio Z2 + daily micro-sequence
- Wed: Upper B + targeted drills
- Thu: Off + micro-sequence
- Fri: Cardio tempo + micro-sequence
- Sat: Upper C + hangboard + post-session mobility
- Sun: Off + light flow and breathing

It runs 12–20 minutes, scalable by phase, and uses circuits, carries, sleds, and low-impact power. Do it after a brief warm-up and only if she’s feeling good from the week. Stop if any shoulder discomfort >2/10.

General rules
- Duration: 12–20 minutes total. Keep RPE around 6–8 depending on phase.
- Format: EMOMs, AMRAPs, or short circuits to keep it engaging.
- Shoulder safety: No overhead lifts, no kipping, no dynamic lock-offs. Neutral/semi-neutral grips, elbows below shoulder height.
- Equipment menu: Sled, bike/erg, trap bar or DBs, kettlebells, sandbag, landmine, med ball for slams to wall at chest height, farmer-carry implements, step/box.

Warm-up (5–7 min)
- 3 min easy bike or brisk walk
- T-spine mobility x6/side, scap push-ups x10, banded ER at 0–30° abd x12/side
- 1–2 rehearsal sets of the circuit with lighter loads

Phase-specific Saturday finisher options
Pick one option each Saturday. Rotate weekly to keep it fresh.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3) — Aerobic strength circuit (12–15 min, RPE 6–7)
- 15-minute continuous circuit, move station-to-station, nasal-breathing pace:
  1) Bike or incline walk: 60s at Z2
  2) Trap-bar or DB rack squat: 10 reps (moderate; keep torso tall)
  3) Chest-supported DB row (neutral): 10 reps
  4) Sled push light-moderate: 20–25 m
  5) Suitcase carry: 20–30 m/side
  6) Pallof press: 8/side
- Notes: Keep mechanics pristine and shoulder relaxed. Skip or reduce any move that provokes symptoms.

Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6) — EMOM power + strength (16 min, RPE 7)
EMOM x16 (4 rounds of 4 stations)
- Min 1: Bike sprint 10–12s hard, then easy spin to minute
- Min 2: Landmine press (below shoulder height) 6–8/side, crisp concentric
- Min 3: Kettlebell hinge (KB deadlift or swing to chest height only if totally symptom-free; otherwise KB deadlift): 12 reps
- Min 4: Chest-supported row 8–10 heavy-ish
Progression: Add a rep or +2–5% load when last round is smooth and pain-free.

Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9) — Mixed modal “engine and grip” (18–20 min, RPE 7–8)
18-minute AMRAP
- Row erg or bike: 12–15 cals (keep shoulders relaxed; on rower use short, neutral stroke if pain-free)
- Sandbag clean to front rack (no shoulder hiking), then reverse lunge alternating: 6/side
- 1-arm KB farmer carry: 30 m R, 30 m L
- Landmine press: 6/side, partial range below shoulder height
- Feet-on hangboard jug/large edge: 10s hang, then step off and shake out
- Chest-supported 1-arm row with 2s pause: 6/side
Scaling: Reduce cals or reps to keep form crisp. If any rowing bothers shoulder, swap for bike.

Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12) — Peak-ready density finisher (12–16 min, RPE 7–8, no grind)
Option A: 12-minute alternating EMOM
- Odd minutes: Sled push 20–30 m heavy but smooth
- Even minutes: Mixed carry complex (1 round per even minute)
  - 20 m double KB farmer carry → 20 m suitcase carry (switch hands halfway)
Keep shoulders down and ribs quiet. Stop any minute early if form slips.

Option B: 4-station density circuit x3 rounds (15–16 min cap)
- A) Assault bike or spin: 45s at strong but sustainable pace
- B) Landmine press 6/side, crisp
- C) Trap-bar deadlift 6–8 moderate-heavy, perfect form
- D) Feet-on hangboard density: 2 x (8–10s hang/15–20s shake) on big edge, then move on
Rest only as needed to keep quality high.

Accessory “fun blocks” menu (plug into any week if time allows, 4–6 min)
- Med-ball chest-height slams to wall: 6–8 reps EMOM x4 (keep ball below shoulder height, catch softly)
- Lateral step-up power: 6/side EMOM x4 (light load, smooth)
- Farmer carry ladder: 20 m light → 20 m moderate → 20 m heavier, 60s rest, repeat once

Safety and coaching cues
- Landmine press: Aim slightly forward in scapular plane, stop well before shoulder height, no pinch.
- Rows: Chest supported when fatigued; avoid end-range anterior glide.
- Carries: “Zip up” ribs, long neck, shoulder blade down and around. Walk tall.
- Sled: Push from midline, neutral wrists, elbows near torso; no leaning hard on right shoulder.

Weekly placement example
- Do the finisher after Saturday’s Upper C session OR as a short standalone if she prefers. Keep it shorter on weeks with very dense hangboard/hard tempo cardio.
- If the week was heavy or shoulder feels “grippy,” choose an easier aerobic circuit (Phase 1 style) or skip and walk.

Auto-regulation
- Green light: 0–2/10 discomfort, resolves within 24h, technique solid.
- Yellow: Any pinch or lingering ache—drop load by 20–30%, shorten duration, swap to bike + carries only.
- Red: Sharp pain, night pain, ROM loss—skip finisher, revert to easy Z2 and mobility, and inform physio.

Here’s the complete 12-week program summary for your 29-year-old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement. All work is pain-free range only, no overhead loading, neutral/semi-neutral grips favored, and progress is via load/density/tempo—not ROM. Coordinate changes with her physio.

Weekly structure
- Strength: 3 upper-body sessions/week (A, B, C)
- Cardio: 2 sessions/week (Z2 + tempo)
- Hangboard/tech prep: Integrated in Phases 2–4 (mostly in Session C or a short standalone)
- Mobility: Daily micro-sequence + targeted drills 2–3x/week
- Saturday finisher: 12–20 min, shoulder-safe, fun conditioning (after Session C)
- Recovery: 7–9 h sleep, hydration, cooldowns, pain rules
- Nutrition: Body recomposition (small deficit), performance-focused timing

Phases at a glance
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Mechanics, scap control, isometrics, horizontal push/pull base. No overhead loading.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Heavier horizontal strength, partial-range landmine press, start hangboard (feet-on, jug/large edge), begin easy technique.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Intensified strength, denser pulling, partial low-angle “vertical” pulls (below shoulder), progressed hangboard density, stronger cardio.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Peak and taper. Highest specific density in Week 10–11, Week 12 taper to arrive fresh for a climbing trip.

Upper-body strength (3 sessions/week)
Session A: Horizontal Pull Emphasis + Cuff/Scap
- Main row pattern (chest-supported rows; neutral grip)
- Low-angle single-arm cable pulldown to chest (elbow below shoulder height; partial vertical)
- Face pull to chest-height (elbows below shoulder)
- Rotator cuff ER (0–45° abduction across phases)
- Scap depression holds; suitcase/farmer carries

Session B: Horizontal Push Emphasis + Row Variations
- DB floor press or low-incline neutral-grip press (pain-free depth)
- Push-up variation (elevation adjusted to comfort)
- Cable fly (low-to-mid, controlled eccentrics, stop short of end range)
- Rotator cuff IR (0–45° abduction across phases)
- Anti-rotation core (Pallof/press holds)

Session C: Unilateral Stability + Climbing Prep
- 1-arm chest-supported rows with pauses
- Landmine press in scapular plane (partial range, below shoulder height)
- Arm work (hammer curls, neutral triceps)
- Forearm/wrist conditioning
- Hangboard/technique block (from Phase 2 onward; feet-on; big holds → large edges)

Key loading and progression
- RPE 6–8 on main lifts; 2–3 reps in reserve, strict technique
- Sets/reps evolve from 4x8–10 (Phase 1 base) to 4–5x4–6 (Phases 3–4 strength), with tempo work (3–4 s eccentrics) and denser rests late in Phase 3
- Progress via reps then load (2–5%); reduce range at first sign of symptoms

Cardio (2x/week)
- Session 1: Long Z2 build
  - Weeks 1–3: 30–40 min
  - Weeks 4–6: 45–55 min
  - Weeks 7–9: 60–70 min
  - Weeks 10–12: 75–90 min (practice fueling: 30–45 g carbs/h + electrolytes)
- Session 2: Tempo/interval endurance
  - Early: Z2 with 1-min surges
  - Mid: 2 x 8–12 min tempo (RPE 6.5–7) with Z2 between
  - Late: 3 x 6–8 min ladders or 2 x 12 min tempo; or hilly Z2

Hangboard and climbing-specific prep (feet-on only unless cleared)
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Intro, 1–2x/week
  - 4–6 x 15–20s feet-on jug/large-edge hangs (RPE 5–6), 60–90s rest
  - 8–12 min easy traverses (slab/vertical), right hand ≤ shoulder height
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Density and endurance, 2x/week
  - Intermittent hangs: 2 rounds of 6–8 x (10–12s on/18–20s off) big edge, 2–3 min between rounds
  - Scap depression/protraction holds on jugs, 3 x 15–20s
  - Optional 6–10 min easy traverses (silent feet, flags)
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–11): Peak-specific density
  - Ladders: 3 ladders of 4 reps each at 8–10s on/12–15s off; 2–3 min between
  - Mixed circuits: jug ↔ big edge (optional medium edge if 100% symptom-free)
- Week 12 taper (Mon only)
  - 2 rounds of 5 x (8–10s on/20–25s off) big edge, RPE 5–6
  - 5–8 min easy technique; zero pump

Mobility (5–6 days/week, 8–12 min)
- Daily micro-sequence: open book, quadruped T-spine rock-backs, scapular CARs, posterior cuff cross-body, low-angle pec doorway, gentle wall slides to tolerated range, breathing reset
- Pre-session: T-spine foam roll, thread-the-needle, scap push-ups, band ER, wall slides
- Post-session: Low-angle pec stretch, posterior cuff, modified sleeper (only if pain-free), breathing
- Targeted 2–3x/week: low-trap raises, serratus roller slides, wall lift-offs, banded scap depression/protraction holds, neck/UT downregulation
- Lower-body/trunk (2–3x/week): hip 90/90, adductor rock-backs, ankle dorsiflexion lunges

Saturday finisher (12–20 min; rotate by phase)
- Phase 1: 15-min aerobic strength circuit (bike/walk, DB rack squat, chest-supported row, sled push, suitcase carry, Pallof)
- Phase 2: 16-min EMOM (bike sprint; landmine press; KB hinge or deadlift; chest-supported row)
- Phase 3: 18-min AMRAP (bike/row cals; sandbag clean to front rack reverse lunges; suitcase carry; landmine press; 10s feet-on hang; 1-arm chest-supported row)
- Phase 4: Density finisher
  - Option A: 12-min alternating EMOM (sled push; mixed carries)
  - Option B: 3-round circuit: bike 45s; landmine press 6/side; trap-bar DL 6–8; feet-on hangboard density micro-set

Nutrition (recomp)
- Calories: Bodyweight x 28–32 kcal/day starting range (small deficit 250–400 kcal)
  - Training days: BW x 30–32; Rest: BW x 28–30; adjust ±100–150 kcal every 2 weeks
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day
- Carbs: 2.5–4.5 g/kg/day, bias around training; intra-carb 15–30 g for long sessions
- Fat: 0.6–1.0 g/kg/day
- Timing: Pre (25–40 g protein + 30–60 g carbs), Post (25–40 g protein + 60–90 g carbs)
- Micros/supps: Collagen 10–15 g + vitamin C 30–60 min pre-rehab/hangs; omega-3 (1–2 g EPA+DHA), vitamin D per labs, creatine 3–5 g/day, hydration 30–35 ml/kg/day + 500–750 ml around training
- Monitoring: 0.25–0.5% BW loss/week, maintain or improve performance, adjust carbs first

Pain rules and substitutions
- Acceptable: 0–2/10 transient discomfort resolving within 24 h
- Not acceptable: Pinch, sharp pain, night pain, ROM loss next day → reduce ROM/load/volume 30–50% and notify physio
- Substitutions:
  - Floor/DB press → machine chest press neutral grip with limited ROM
  - Landmine press → cable press at chest height or isometric wall press
  - Chest-supported row → machine row with chest pad/neutral handles
  - Face pull → cable ER to chest-height

Peak/taper (Weeks 10–12 highlight)
- Week 10–11: Heaviest strength and hangboard density; cardio long Z2 75–80 min; fuel at or near maintenance on long days
- Week 12: Early-week primer only (short strength + light hang density + easy technique), then rest, hydrate, and increase carbs to maintenance/slight surplus. Begin climbing trip fresh.

Weekly layout example
- Mon: Upper A + mobility
- Tue: Cardio Z2 + mobility
- Wed: Upper B + targeted mobility
- Thu: Hangboard/technique short block or rest + mobility
- Fri: Cardio tempo/hills + mobility
- Sat: Upper C + hangboard/technique + finisher + post-session mobility
- Sun: Off/easy walk + breathing/mobility

This integrated plan builds upper-body strength safely, restores shoulder mechanics, develops aerobic and grip endurance, and peaks her capacity for Week 12 while protecting the right shoulder. Adjust loads/volume weekly to keep symptoms at zero and performance trending up.
